record.title: Godara–Sarkar conjecture for the small Davenport constant of Heisenberg groups
record.statement: Godara and Sarkar conjectured that, for every odd prime $p$, if $H_{p^3}=\operatorname{UT}_3(\mathbb{F}_p)$ is the Heisenberg group of order $p^3$, then $\mathsf{d}(H_{p^3})=3p-3$, where $\mathsf{d}(G)$ is the maximum length of a sequence over a finite group $G$ having no nonempty subsequence whose terms can be ordered to have product equal to the identity.
record.references: - [The small Davenport constant of the Heisenberg group of order 343](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13747) — arXiv — Andreas Volkmann

record.title: Transposition diameter problem
record.statement: For a permutation $\pi\in S_n$, let $d_T(\pi,\iota)$ be the minimum number of transpositions whose product sends $\pi$ to the identity permutation $\iota$. Define the transposition diameter by $TD(n)=\max_{\pi\in S_n}d_T(\pi,\iota)$. Determine the exact value of $TD(16)$. The cited preprint claims that $TD(16)=9$.
record.references: - [Twisted Bracelets for Sorting by Transpositions: the Transposition Diameter of S_{16}](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17493) — arXiv — Luiz A. G. Silva, Luis A. B. Kowada, Noraí R. Rocco, Maria E. M. T. Walter

record.title: Model-RB frb100-40 maximum-independent-set challenge
record.statement: Let $G_{\mathrm{frb100\text{-}40}}=(V,E)$ be the publicly specified $4{,}000$-vertex Model-RB benchmark graph. Determine its independence number $\alpha(G_{\mathrm{frb100\text{-}40}})$, equivalently find a set $S\subseteq V$ of maximum cardinality such that for all distinct $u,v\in S$, $\{u,v\}\notin E$. The reported certificate claims that $\alpha(G_{\mathrm{frb100\text{-}40}})=100$.
record.references: - [frb100-40 After Two Decades: An Optimality Certificate and a Preregistered Search Study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.02804) — arXiv

record.title: Erdős Problem 848
record.statement: Determine whether the following sharp upper-density bound holds: if $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ satisfies $ab+1$ is not squarefree for every $a,b\in A$, then $\overline{d}(A):=\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac{|A\cap\{1,\ldots,N\}|}{N}\leq\frac{1}{25}$. The bound is sharp, since $A=\{n\in\mathbb{N}:n\equiv 7\pmod{25}\}$ satisfies $ab+1\equiv 0\pmod{25}$ for all $a,b\in A$.
record.references: - [Erdős 848 squarefree product](https://github.com/crabsatellite/erdos-848-squarefree-product) — GitHub

record.title: Integer relative Heffter-array existence problem

record.title: Erdős problem #396
record.statement: For each integer $k\ge 1$, determine the smallest integer $n\ge k$ such that $n(n-1)(n-2)\cdots(n-k)$ divides the central binomial coefficient $\binom{2n}{n}$; equivalently, determine $n_k=\min\{n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge k}:\prod_{j=0}^{k}(n-j)\mid\binom{2n}{n}\}$ whenever this set is nonempty.

record.title: Spearman rho–footrule region problem
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be the set of bivariate copulas, equivalently the set of joint laws of random variables $U,V\sim\mathcal{U}(0,1)$. Define Spearman's rho and Spearman's footrule by $\rho_S(U,V)=12\mathbb{E}[UV]-3$ and $\phi_S(U,V)=1-6\mathbb{E}[|U-V|]$. Determine exactly the attainable region $\mathcal{R}=\{(\phi_S(U,V),\rho_S(U,V)):(U,V)\text{ has a bivariate copula law}\}$. Equivalently, for every $x\in[-\tfrac12,1]$, determine the extremal values, in particular $\sup\{\rho_S(U,V):\phi_S(U,V)=x\}$, and hence the exact upper and lower boundaries of $\mathcal{R}$.
record.references: - [The exact Spearman rho-footrule region via optimal transport](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.20176) — arXiv

record.title: Real-rootedness classification for refined Narayana polynomials
record.statement: For every pair of integers $1\le k\le n$, consider the refined Narayana polynomial and its formal degree-$k$ symmetric decomposition, written in the form $F_{n,k}(t)=a_{n,k}(t)+t\,b_{n,k}(t)$. The problem is to determine exactly for which pairs $(n,k)$ the polynomials $a_{n,k}(t)$ and the coefficientwise absolute-value polynomial $|b_{n,k}(t)|$ are real-rooted, according to Conjecture 36 of Bóna et al. The supplied source reports that the published classification fails at $(n,k)=(3,3)$: there $a_{3,3}(t)=(1+t)(1+t^2)$ and $|b_{3,3}(t)|=1+t+t^2$, neither of which is real-rooted. A boundary-corrected classification has been proposed, but its general proof has not been independently verified.

record.title: Uniqueness of the -primitive decomposition for fixed square-free part
record.statement: Let $s\in\mathbb{N}$ be square-free, and let $P(s)$ be the set of $\Delta$-primitives with square-free part $s$. A natural number $n$ has a **$\Delta$-primitive decomposition** if it can be written as $n=\alpha^2m$ with $\alpha\in\mathbb{N}$ and $m$ $\Delta$-primitive. **Fixed-square-free-part uniqueness conjecture.** If $|P(s)|=1$, then every non-square $n\in\mathbb{N}(\Delta)$ with square-free part $s$ admits a unique $\Delta$-primitive decomposition. The conjecture refines a uniqueness question that is false in general: the paper gives $5616=3^2\cdot624=2^2\cdot1404$ as the smallest counterexample, while the classification of integers with multiple decompositions remains open.
record.source_name: Victor N. Schvöllner, “The Δ property: a bridge between split graphs and Number Theory”, arXiv:2605.25264 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.25264

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of May 2026).

solutions.body:
**Complete proof.** For a positive integer \(u=\prod_p p^{e_p}\), let
\[
\operatorname{sf}(u)=\prod_{e_p\text{ odd}}p
\]
denote its square-free part. For every positive integer \(c\),
\[
\operatorname{sf}(c^2u)=\operatorname{sf}(u).
\]

Proposition 3.2 of the source establishes that every \(n\in\mathbb N(\Delta)\) admits a decomposition \(n=c^2m\), where \(c\ge1\) and \(m\) is \(\Delta\)-primitive. Equivalently, repeatedly remove a nontrivial square factor whenever its quotient remains in \(\mathbb N(\Delta)\). The positive quotients strictly decrease, so the process terminates at a primitive quotient.

Fix a square-free \(s\) with \(|P(s)|=1\), and suppose \(n\in\mathbb N(\Delta)\) has square-free part \(s\). If
\[
n=c_1^2m_1=c_2^2m_2
\]
are primitive decompositions, square-free-part invariance gives
\[
\operatorname{sf}(m_1)=\operatorname{sf}(n)=s=\operatorname{sf}(m_2).
\]
Thus \(m_1,m_2\in P(s)\). Since \(P(s)\) is a singleton, \(m_1=m_2\); consequently \(c_1^2=c_2^2\), and positivity gives \(c_1=c_2\). The decomposition therefore exists and is unique. The nonsquare assumption is unnecessary.

More precisely, writing \(n=su^2\), its primitive decompositions are in bijection with
\[
\{d\mid u:sd^2\in P(s)\}
\]
via \(m=sd^2\) and \(c=u/d\). Conversely, if \(P(s)\) contains distinct \(m_i=sd_i^2\), then
\[
N=s\,\operatorname{lcm}(d_1,d_2)^2
\]
has two distinct primitive decompositions, and every square multiple of \(N\) does as well. For \(s>1\), all these examples are nonsquares.

record.title: WoTW 160
record.statement: WOWII [Conjecture 160](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/) For a simple connected graph $G$, $L_s(G) \ge \max_v l(v) + \max_v T(v) \cdot \chi_{C_4}(G)$ where: - $L_s(G) = \mathrm{SimpleGraph.Ls}\, G$ is the maximum number of leaves over all spanning trees of $G$, - $\max_v l(v)$ is the maximum local independence number over vertices, - $\max_v T(v)$ is the maximum number of triangles incident to any vertex, - $\chi_{C_4}(G)$ is `1` if $G$ has no cycle of length four and `0` otherwise. A formal proof uses the $C_4$-free neighborhood identity $d(v) = \lambda(v) + T(v)$ with a star/geodesic case analysis, routed through the connected-seed spanning-tree bound developed for Conjecture 2. An independent second proof, via a closest maximizer pair joined by a shortest path, is linked from the pull request that recorded the solution.

record.title: Albertson–Berman conjecture on induced forests in planar graphs
record.statement: For every simple planar graph $G$ with $n=|V(G)|$ vertices, if $a(G)$ denotes the maximum number of vertices in an induced forest of $G$, then $a(G)\geq \frac{n}{2}$.
record.references: - [A counterexample to the Albertson-Berman conjecture about induced forests in planar graphs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13964) — arXiv — Mikhail Makarov

record.title: Kusner’s conjecture on equilateral sets in ℓ_p^n
record.statement: For every integer $n\geq 1$ and every real $p$ satisfying $2<p<\infty$, the maximum cardinality of an equilateral set in $\ell_p^n$ is $e(\ell_p^n)=n+1$. Equivalently, every set $X\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ whose distinct points have pairwise $\ell_p$-distance $1$ has at most $n+1$ elements.
record.references: - [A counterexample to Kusner's conjecture on equilateral sets](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.14013) — arXiv — Logan R. Chalmers

record.title: Erdős Problem #696 (normal-order conjecture)
record.statement: Determine the normal orders of the arithmetic functions $h(n)$ and $H(n)$. The supplied source identifies this as Erdős Problem $\#696$, but does not define $h$, $H$, or specify the claimed normal-order functions precisely enough to state the conjecture in full.

record.title: Domination–packing inequality $\gamma(G)\le2\rho(G)+1$
record.statement: For every connected graph $G$ with maximum degree $\Delta(G)\le 3$, the domination number satisfies $\gamma(G)\le 2\rho(G)+1$, where $\rho(G)$ is the maximum cardinality of a set of vertices whose pairwise distances are at least $3$.
record.references: - [New lower bounds on domination--packing ratios in connected subcubic and cubic graphs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15525) — arXiv — JiSun Huh, Juho Kim

record.title: Bickle’s conjecture on collapsible graphs
record.statement: For every pair of integers $k\ge 3$ and $n\ge k+1$, the minimum of $\left|\{v\in V(G):\deg_G(v)=k\}\right|$ over all graphs $G$ of order $n$ satisfying $\delta(G)=k$ and $\delta(H)<k$ for every nonempty proper induced subgraph $H$ of $G$ is $\max\left\{\left\lceil\frac{2n}{2k-1}\right\rceil,\,k^2-k-2-(k-3)n\right\}$, where such a graph is called $k$-collapsible.
record.references: - [A proof of Bickle's conjecture on collapsible graphs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15629) — arXiv — Xingzhi Zhan

record.title: Erdős problem 647
record.statement: Determine whether there exists an integer $n>24$ such that $\max_{1\le m<n}\bigl(m+\tau(m)\bigr)\le n+2$, where $\tau(m)$ denotes the number of positive divisors of $m$. Equivalently, the conjecture asserts that no such $n$ exists.
record.references: - [A Kernel-Checked Exclusion Certificate for Erdős Problem 647](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.17880) — arXiv — David Turean

record.title: Erdős four-edge intersection problem
record.statement: For an $n$-vertex graph $G$ and a permutation $\sigma$ of its vertex set, define $I_G(\sigma)=|E(G)\cap E(\sigma(G))|$, and let $f(n,4)$ be the minimum possible value of $|E(G)|$ over all $n$-vertex graphs satisfying $I_G(\sigma)\ge 4$ for every permutation $\sigma$. The problem asks whether, for all sufficiently large integers $n$, $f(n,4)=2n-4$.
record.references: - [An asymptotic solution to the Erdős four-edge intersection problem](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.17727) — arXiv — Peter Keevash, Benny Sudakov

record.title: Albertson–Berman conjecture
record.statement: For every simple planar graph $G$ with $n=|V(G)|$ vertices, there exists a set $S\subseteq V(G)$ such that the induced subgraph $G[S]$ is a forest and $|S|\ge n/2$. Equivalently, if $a(G)$ denotes the maximum number of vertices in an induced forest of $G$, then $a(G)\ge n/2$.
record.references: - [A 15/31 Counterexample Family to the Albertson-Berman Conjecture](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.17350) — arXiv — David Eppstein, Dmitry Karpov

record.title: Kashima’s pancyclicity analogue conjecture
record.statement: For every integer $n\ge 4$, every $2$-connected graph $G$ of order $n$ with minimum degree $\delta(G)\ge \sqrt{3n}$ contains a $2$-connected subgraph of every order $\ell\in\{4,5,\ldots,n\}$.
record.references: - [A Sublinear Minimum-Degree Condition for 2-Connected Subgraphs of All Orders](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.17478) — arXiv

record.title: Guerra–Tione Question 5.5 on gradient mappings
record.statement: For each dimension $n\ge 2$, determine whether the following implication holds: for every domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^{n}$, every $u\in W^{2,n}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$, and every constant $\delta>0$, if $\det D^{2}u\ge\delta$ almost everywhere in $\Omega$, then the gradient mapping $Du:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}^{n}$ is open and discrete.

record.title: Lin–Zhao graph Steklov eigenvalue problem
record.statement: Does there exist a universal constant $C>0$ such that, for every connected graph $G=(V,E)$ with boundary $B$, maximum degree $d_{\max}$, and genus $g$, one has $\sigma_k(G,B)\leq C d_{\max}\frac{g+k}{|B|}$ for every integer $k$ satisfying $1\leq k\leq |B|$, where $\sigma_k(G,B)$ is the $k$-th Steklov eigenvalue of $G$ with boundary $B$?
record.references: - [A transfer principle for Steklov eigenvalue estimates of graphs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.17264) — arXiv

record.title: Ramsey number R(4,20)
record.statement: Determine the exact value of the Ramsey number $R(4,20)$, defined by $R(4,20)=\min\{n\in\mathbb{N}:\text{ every graph on }n\text{ vertices contains either a copy of }K_4\text{ or an independent set of }20\text{ vertices}\}$.

record.title: Endpoint Nevanlinna defect problem
record.statement: Determine whether, for every countable family of hyperplanes $\{H_j\}_{j\in\mathbb{N}}$ in general position in $\mathbb{P}^m$ and every linearly nondegenerate holomorphic curve $f\colon\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{P}^m$ of finite lower order, the Nevanlinna defects satisfy $\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\delta_f(H_j)^{1/3}<\infty$.

record.title: Broadcast domination conjecture
record.statement: For every connected graph $G$, the broadcast domination number is at most twice the multipacking number: $\gamma_b(G)\leq 2\operatorname{mp}(G)$, where $\gamma_b(G)$ is the minimum cost of a dominating broadcast on $G$ and $\operatorname{mp}(G)$ is the maximum cardinality of a multipacking in $G$.

record.title: Lichiardopol’s conjecture
record.statement: $\exists g:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}\ \forall k\in\mathbb{N}\ \forall D\ \bigl(\delta^+(D)\ge g(k)\ \Longrightarrow\ \exists C_1,\ldots,C_k\text{ vertex-disjoint directed cycles in }D\text{ such that }|C_i|\ne|C_j|\text{ for all }i\ne j\bigr)$, where $\delta^+(D)$ denotes the minimum out-degree of $D$.
record.references: - [Proof of Lichiardopol's conjecture on disjoint directed cycles of distinct lengths](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.20012) — arXiv

record.title: Bandeira–Kireeva–Maillard–Rödder Kuramoto conjecture
record.statement: For every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a finite simple graph $G$ on $n$ vertices such that $\delta(G)\geq (3/4-\varepsilon)n$ and $G$ is not globally synchronizing for the Kuramoto model; equivalently, the Kuramoto energy on $G$ has a local minimum other than a fully synchronized state.
record.references: - [Graphs with connectivity 3/4 - ε are globally synchronizing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.20010) — arXiv

record.title: OEIS A080170 conjecture
record.statement: For every integer $k\ge 2$, the binomial-coefficient gcd quantity $D(k)$ specified in OEIS A080170 satisfies $D(k)=1$ if and only if $\frac{k+1}{\operatorname{ppart}(k+1)}>\operatorname{ppart}(k+1)$, where $\operatorname{ppart}(n)=\max\{p^a:p\text{ is prime and }p^a\mathrel{\|}n\}$ is the largest exact prime-power component of $n$.
record.references: - [Formal Conjectures issue 4252](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/issues/4252) — GitHub

record.title: Henning–Yeo conjecture on identifying vertex covers
record.statement: For every finite graph $G$ with order $n=|V(G)|$, size $m=|E(G)|$, and maximum degree $\Delta=\Delta(G)$, does the identifying vertex cover number of $G$ satisfy the upper-bound inequality conjectured by Henning and Yeo in terms of $n$, $m$, and $\Delta$?
record.references: - [Connected Counterexamples to the Henning--Yeo Conjecture on Identifying Vertex Covers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19455) — arXiv — Wang, Yufeng

record.title: Minimum length of a superpermutation
record.statement: A superpermutation on $n$ symbols is a string containing every permutation of the $n$ symbols as a contiguous substring. Determine the minimum possible length of a superpermutation for every $n>5$.

record.title: Chromatic-polynomial/list-color-function persistence conjecture
record.statement: For every finite graph $G$ and every integer $k\ge 1$, if $P(G,k)=P_{\ell}(G,k)>0$, then $P(G,k+1)=P_{\ell}(G,k+1)$, where $P(G,k)$ is the number of proper $k$-colorings of $G$ and $P_{\ell}(G,k)=\min_{L}|\{\text{proper }L\text{-colorings of }G\}|$ is the minimum, over all assignments $L$ of lists of $k$ colors to the vertices of $G$, of the number of proper $L$-colorings.
record.references: - [Non-persistence of equality between chromatic polynomials and list-color functions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19773) — arXiv — Zhang, Meiqiao, Dong, Fengming

record.title: Generalized rational exponents conjecture
record.statement: For every rational number $\alpha\ge 1$, there exist fixed finite simple graphs $H_\alpha$ and $F_\alpha$ such that, as $n\to\infty$, the maximum number of copies of $H_\alpha$ in an $n$-vertex graph containing no copy of $F_\alpha$ satisfies $\operatorname{ex}(n,H_\alpha,F_\alpha)=\Theta(n^\alpha)$.
record.references: - [On the Generalized Rational Exponents Conjecture](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19923) — arXiv — Hou, Jianfeng, Yang, Caihong

record.title: Growth rate of Av(1324)
record.statement: Determine the exact value of the Stanley–Wilf limit $\operatorname{gr}(\operatorname{Av}(1324)):=\lim_{n\to\infty}\lvert\operatorname{Av}_n(1324)\rvert^{1/n}$, where $\operatorname{Av}_n(1324)$ is the set of permutations of length $n$ containing no subsequence order-isomorphic to the pattern $1324$.
record.references: - [A new lower bound for the growth rate of Av(1324)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.20292) — arXiv — Norton, Charles C.

record.title: Bao–Wulan multiplier problem for QK spaces
record.statement: For the Möbius-invariant space $Q_K$ on the unit disc, determine whether the pointwise multiplier algebra satisfies $\mathcal{M}(Q_K)=H^\infty\cap Q_K^{\log}$, where $\mathcal{M}(Q_K)=\{g:g f\in Q_K\text{ for every }f\in Q_K\text{ and }f\mapsto gf\text{ is bounded on }Q_K\}$ and $Q_K^{\log}$ is the logarithmic $Q_K$-class specified in the Bao–Wulan formulation.
record.references: - [Carleson measures, Volterra integral operators and multipliers for QK spaces](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.20205) — arXiv

record.title: Zhuang–Gao conjecture
record.statement: For every finite nonabelian group $G$, the Gao constant satisfies $E(G)=\mathsf d(G)+|G|$, where $\mathsf d(G)$ is the largest integer $\ell$ for which there exists a product-one-free sequence over $G$ of length $\ell$, and $E(G)$ is the least integer $\ell$ such that every sequence over $G$ of length at least $\ell$ contains a product-one subsequence of length exactly $|G|$.
record.references: - [The Gao-Zhuang conjecture for the Heisenberg group](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23319) — arXiv

record.title: Open group-specific existence problems for signed difference sets
record.statement: Given a finite abelian group $G$ of order $v$ and integers $k$ and $\lambda$, determine whether there exists a function $x:G\to\{-1,0,1\}$ such that $\sum_{g\in G}x(g)^2=k$ and, for every nonzero $h\in G$, $\sum_{g\in G}x(g)x(g+h)=\lambda$. Equivalently, determine which finite abelian groups admit a signed difference set with prescribed parameters $(v,k,\lambda)$.
record.references: - [Nonexistence Results and Constructions for Signed Difference Sets](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.22936) — arXiv

record.title: Gerbner–Győri–Methuku–Vizer generalized Turán conjecture
record.statement:
For all integers $l>k\ge 2$, let $\mathscr{C}_{2k}=\{C_3,C_4,\ldots,C_{2k}\}$. Then
$$\operatorname{ex}\bigl(n,C_{2k+1},\mathscr{C}_{2k}\cup\{C_{2l+1}\}\bigr)=o(n^2)\qquad\text{as }n\to\infty,$$
where $\operatorname{ex}(n,H,\mathcal{F})$ is the maximum number of copies of $H$ in an $n$-vertex graph containing no member of $\mathcal{F}$, and $C_i$ denotes the cycle of length $i$.
record.references: - [A subquadratic bound for generalized Turán numbers of odd cycles](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.22893) — arXiv

record.title: Gao–Wu–Xue treewidth conjecture for generalized Turán problems
record.statement: For every integer $r\ge 3$ and every finite graph $F$ satisfying $\chi(F)=r$ and $\operatorname{tw}(F)\ge r$, there exist constants $c_F>0$ and $n_0(F)$ such that, for every integer $n\ge n_0(F)$, $\operatorname{ex}(n,K_r,F)\ge c_F n^{r-1}$, where $\operatorname{ex}(n,K_r,F)$ denotes the maximum number of copies of $K_r$ in an $n$-vertex $F$-free graph.
record.references: - [Counterexamples to a treewidth conjecture on generalized Turán problems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.22742) — arXiv

record.title: Riemann Hypothesis via Weil’s positivity criterion
record.statement: Determine whether $\lambda^*(L)\ge 0$ for every $L>0$, where $\lambda^*(L)=\inf\left\{Q(f)/\lVert f\rVert_2^2:0\ne f,\ \operatorname{supp}f\subseteq[-L,L]\right\}$ and $Q$ is Weil’s quadratic form. Equivalently, determine whether $Q(f)\ge 0$ for every admissible compactly supported test function $f$; by Weil’s criterion, this is equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis.
record.references: - [Weil positivity in compact windows: certified two-sided bounds and a Landau--Widom decay law](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24827) — arXiv

record.title: Strong maximum principle conjecture for higher-order GJMS operators
record.statement: For every closed Riemannian manifold $(M^n,g)$ with $n\ge 7$, if $Q_g^{(2)}>0$, $Q_g^{(4)}>0$, $Q_g^{(6)}>0$, and the sixth-order GJMS operator $P_{6,g}$ is strictly positive as a self-adjoint operator, then $P_{6,g}$ has a positive Green function; equivalently, the associated sixth-order equation satisfies the strong maximum principle.
record.references: - [A counterexample to a strong maximum principle for the sixth-order GJMS operator](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24148) — arXiv

record.title: Optimal leading coefficient problem for AWGN spherical codes
record.statement: For every pair of integers $n,k$ satisfying $3\leq k\leq n-1$, the optimal leading coefficient in the high-SNR maximum-likelihood error-probability expansion for SNR-dependent $(n+k,n)$ AWGN spherical codes is conjectured to satisfy $K_{n+k,n}^{\ast}=4k(k-1)$, where $K_{n+k,n}^{\ast}$ denotes the SNR-wise optimal coefficient.
record.references: - [Beyond Minimum Distance: The Optimal Leading Coefficient in the High-SNR Error-Probability Expansion for AWGN Spherical Codes](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25805) — arXiv

record.title: Adm–Fallat–Meagher–Nasserasr–Plosker–Yang question on MB(\overline{P_n})
record.statement: For a graph $G$, let $\mathcal{S}(G)$ be the set of real symmetric matrices whose off-diagonal zero–nonzero pattern is the adjacency pattern of $G$. Define $MB(G)$ to be the minimum, over all $A\in\mathcal{S}(G)$ having exactly two distinct eigenvalues, of the smaller of their two multiplicities. Determine $MB(\overline{P_n})$ for every integer $n\ge 8$, where $P_n$ is the path on $n$ vertices.
record.references: - [Rank-Three Projections and Minimal Multiplicity Bipartitions of Path Complements](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27227) — arXiv

record.title: Maximum number of circles tangent to three conics
record.statement: Determine the maximum number of distinct real circles tangent to each of three general real conics in the Euclidean plane. The proposed conjecture was that every such triple has at most $136$ real tritangent circles, with an explicit configuration attaining $136$; the 2026 preprint claims a configuration with $144$.
record.references: - [144 real circles tangent to three conics](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01521) — arXiv

record.title: Ramsey threshold for trees versus odd cycles
record.statement: For an odd integer $m\ge 3$, determine the least integer $f(m)$ such that, for every integer $n\ge f(m)$ and every tree $T_n$ on $n$ vertices, the Ramsey number satisfies $R(T_n,C_m)=2n-1$. The conjectured exact value is $f(m)=\left\lceil\frac{2m-1}{3}\right\rceil$ for every odd $m\ge 5$.
record.references: - [The Ramsey threshold for trees versus odd cycles](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.00944) — arXiv
